messages.author: 58ecca54321bc805
messages.subject: Various reference.fasta issues
parts:
I am working with some TCGA data and the bams use various reference.fasta files. I am trying to set up the gc50 file but receive a KeyError 'M'. The issue seems to be this line in the GRCh37-lite.fa

CGCTACATAGCTGMCTTATTATTCGTGGTCCCCTATGACCCCCTGATCATTTTCCCTGAG

I am not sure what is the best solution to overcome this error. I assume some sort of exception needs to be added to sequenza-utils GC-window but I do not know what would be the best course of action without breaking things. Any suggestions?

-bwubb

messages.author: 58ecca54321bc805
messages.subject: Re: Various reference.fasta issues
parts:
I would like to ask too, if it truly matters what gc50Base file is used? I did not think that there was that much difference between hg19 and GRCh37. Perhaps I could just use the exampled hg19.gc50Base.txt.gz (changing the chr as needed)?

-bwubb

parts:
Hi Brad,

I'm sorry to hear that, I though I fixed the problem with this commit:

https://bitbucket.org/ffavero/sequenza/diff/exec/sequenza-utils.py?diff2=b953cae8c217&at=dnorm

If you still have an earlier version of the python script you could try to replace the script with the one in the R library folder, or take the latest version from bitbucket:

https://bitbucket.org/ffavero/sequenza/raw/7527521e69c05540fe3f0a0e7ec39a8b82613e27/exec/sequenza-utils.py

Let me know if this solve it, otherwise I'll have to fix it again.

About your second question... I think both hg19 and GRCh37 are based on the same genome reversion (I would't to say blasphemy, but I think nothing major is changing). So it would be perfectly fine if you just change the chromosome names (removing the "chr").

Thanks!

(PS: sorry Brad for the duplicate message, I forgot "reply to all" to include the reply in the mailing list...)
